preamble: The glottal stop [ʔ] is replaced by the palatal glide [j], typically next to front vowels or in hiatus where the glide is the natural transition. Assyrian Neo-Aramaic turned inherited word-initial /ʔ/ into /j/ in most dialects, and Levantine Arabic replaced Classical Arabic medial hamza after long ā with y in active participles such as nāʔim > nāyim 'sleeping'.

examples.note: Initial /ʔ/ became /j/ in most dialects; compare Turoyo ܝܰܪܝܟ݂ܐ (yarixo) and Hebrew אָרֹךְ ('arókh).
Same shift of initial /ʔ/ to /j/; the word goes back to Proto-Semitic *ʔahl- 'tent camp'.
Hamza after long ā in the active participle is replaced by y.
